translations.text: Paul, a servant of God and an apostle of Jesus Christ, according to the faith of God’s chosen people and the knowledge of the truth that accords with godliness,
in the hope of eternal life, which God, who does not lie, promised before the ages began.
But at the appointed times he revealed his word through preaching, with which I was entrusted according to the command of God our Savior.
To Titus, a beloved son according to our common faith: grace and peace from God the Father and Christ Jesus our Savior.
For this very reason I left you in Crete, so that you might set right whatever was lacking and appoint elders in each city, as I instructed you.
If anyone is blameless, the husband of one wife, and has believing children who are not accused of reckless living or disobedient,
for a bishop must be blameless as God’s steward, not arrogant, not quick-tempered, not abusive, not violent, not greedy for dishonest gain,
but hospitable, a lover of goodness, humble, just, holy, and self-controlled.
An overseer is to be faithful to the word of teaching, so that he may be able both to encourage with sound teaching and to rebuke those who oppose it.
For there are many who are disobedient, empty talkers and deceivers, especially those who belong to the circumcision.
They must be silenced, since they ruin entire households and teach what they ought not to teach for the sake of dishonest gain.
One of them, their own prophet, said, “Cretans are always liars, wicked troublemakers, lazy good-for-nothings.”
This testimony is true. Therefore rebuke them very sternly, so that they may become sound in faith
and not pay attention to Jewish myths and the commands of people who have turned away from the truth.
Everything is pure to the pure, but to the defiled and unbelieving nothing is pure; rather, their minds and thoughts are defiled.
They profess to know God, but deny him by their deeds. They are defiled and disobedient, unfit for any good work.
But you, speak what is fitting for sound teaching.
Older men should be sober, dignified, humble, sound in faith, in love, in patience, and in self-control.
Older women likewise should be sober and conduct themselves with holy propriety, not slanderers or addicted to wine, but teachers of what is good,
so that they may teach the young women to be sensible, to love their husbands and their children,
to be humble, pure, attentive to their households, doing good, and obedient to their own husbands, so that God’s word and teaching may not be blasphemed.
Likewise, urge the young men to be humble,
setting yourself before everyone as an example of good works, maintaining integrity, holiness, and dignity in your teaching,
and sound speech that cannot be condemned, so that an opponent may be put to shame and have nothing evil to say about us.
Servants should be obedient to their own masters and please them in everything, not contradicting them.
Not pilfering, but showing complete faithfulness with goodness, so that in everything they may adorn the teaching of God our Savior.
For the grace of God has appeared, bringing salvation to all people,
teaching us to renounce ungodliness and worldly desires and to live soberly, righteously, and devoutly in this world.
And let us await the blessed hope and the appearance of the glory of the great God and our Savior Jesus Christ.
Who gave himself for us, so that he might redeem us from all lawlessness and purify for himself a people of his own, zealous for good works.
Speak these things, encourage, and rebuke with all authority, so that no one despises you.
Remind them to be obedient and subject to rulers and authorities, and to be ready for every good work.
They must slander no one, avoid quarrels, be gentle, and show all humility toward everyone.
For we too were once foolish, disobedient, and led astray. We were slaves to desires and various excesses, living in malice and envy, hated and hating one another.
But when the kindness and love for humanity of God our Savior appeared,
he saved us, not because of righteous works that we had done, but according to his mercy, through the washing of rebirth and renewal by the Holy Spirit,
whom he poured out abundantly upon us through Jesus Christ our Savior,
so that, justified by grace, we might become heirs in the hope of eternal life.

This saying is trustworthy, and I want you to insist on these things, so that those who have believed in God will take care to devote themselves to good works. These things are good and useful for people.
But reject foolish questions, genealogies, disputes, and quarrels about the law, for they are useless and empty.
Reject a person who causes divisions after warning him once and then a second time.
Know that such a person has gone astray and sins, condemning himself.
When I send Artemas or Tychicus to you, hurry to come to me at Nicopolis, for I have decided to spend the winter there.
Send Zenas, the expert in the law, and Apollos on their way promptly, so that they lack nothing.
Let our people also learn to devote themselves to good works to meet pressing needs, so that they will not be unfruitful.

Everyone who is with me sends you greetings. Greet those who love us in the faith. Grace be with you all. To Titus, ordained the first bishop of the church of the Cretans. Written from Nicopolis in Macedonia.
